source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Macroeconomics, Ch. 6 (Open Economy Macroeconomics).

sections.heading: 1. Open Economy and Balance of Payments
points: An **open economy** trades with the rest of the world (exports, imports, capital flows).
The **Balance of Payments (BoP)** = a systematic record of all economic transactions between a country's residents and the rest of the world.
Two accounts: the **Current Account** (trade in goods/services, income, transfers) and the **Capital Account** (capital flows — investment, loans).

sections.heading: 2. Current and Capital Account
points: **Current Account** = **balance of trade (goods) + services (invisibles) + net income + net transfers**.
**Trade balance** = exports − imports of goods (surplus if exports > imports).
**Capital Account** = foreign investment (FDI/FPI), external borrowing, etc.
**BoP deficit/surplus** — the overall balance; accommodated by changes in **foreign exchange reserves**.

sections.heading: 3. Foreign Exchange Rate
points: **Exchange rate** = the price of one currency in terms of another (e.g. ₹ per $).

sub: **Fixed exchange rate** — set/pegged by the government/central bank.
**Flexible (floating) exchange rate** — determined by market demand and supply of currency.
**Managed floating** — market-determined but with central bank intervention (India's system).

points: **Depreciation** = a fall in the currency's value (flexible system); **Devaluation** = a deliberate reduction (fixed system).

sections.heading: 4. Determination and Effects
points: The exchange rate is determined by the **demand and supply of foreign currency** (from trade and capital flows).
A **depreciating rupee** makes exports cheaper (boosts them) and imports costlier.
Exchange rate changes affect trade, inflation, and capital flows.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: BoP = record of transactions with the rest of the world (current + capital accounts).
Current account = trade + services (invisibles) + income + transfers.
Capital account = investment, borrowing (capital flows).
Exchange rate systems: fixed, flexible (floating), managed floating (India).
Depreciation (market fall) vs devaluation (deliberate, fixed system).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Current account = trade + invisibles (services/income/transfers)**; **capital account = capital flows**.
**Depreciation = market-driven fall**; **devaluation = deliberate reduction** (fixed system).
India follows a **managed floating** exchange rate.
A **weaker rupee makes exports cheaper and imports costlier**.
